tokens.name: --current
tokens.note: Meaning. Coral is "now" and nothing else -- GPS was cut for time, so it has no live use in the app and stays reserved rather than becoming decoration. Teal is zones. tokens.name: --tap-min
tokens.note: Two tap-size rules (Ernest, 10/6; 44 CSS px = 44pt on iPhone, Apple's HIG minimum). --tap-min the floor for every CONTROL: chips, the sheet's close, the zoom buttons, the ItemPager's buttons. It replaces the 40px floor the zoom stack and the ItemPager used to sit on. --pin-hit the invisible hit area centred on every map pin. The visible marker (--pin-size) is unchanged; MapCanvas draws this circle and the e2e no-overlap rule measures it, at every stop.

tokens.name: --pin-hit
tokens.note: Two tap-size rules (Ernest, 10/6; 44 CSS px = 44pt on iPhone, Apple's HIG minimum). --tap-min the floor for every CONTROL: chips, the sheet's close, the zoom buttons, the ItemPager's buttons. It replaces the 40px floor the zoom stack and the ItemPager used to sit on. --pin-hit the invisible hit area centred on every map pin. The visible marker (--pin-size) is unchanged; MapCanvas draws this circle and the e2e no-overlap rule measures it, at every stop.

tokens.name: --pin-size
tokens.note: 40px, not the 28px the draft spec proposed: judged against the real map, where 28 read as too small. The tap area is 44 either way. ONE size at every zoom level: the overview used to draw pins a step smaller (34), and a pinch that crossed the overview boundary ended with every pin popping to a new size the moment the fingers lifted (Ernest, iPhone, 9/19). A pin is a control, not ground; it holds one on-screen size while the map scales under it, gesture and settle included.

tokens.name: --sheet-peek-height
tokens.note: The short detent (B3): about the title row plus one or two lines. A sheet that opens while a filter chip is on opens this tall, so the map stays visible; the handle (drag up, or tap) takes it to --sheet-max-height.

tokens.name: --sheet-detail-min-height
tokens.note: A booth's detail sheet never gets shorter than this, whatever the booth's text: stepping through a run must not change the sheet's height, or the ItemPager's buttons move under the thumb (B2). Sized so the longest booth entry at 375px fits above the footer without scrolling.

tokens.name: --map-inset-top
tokens.note: The map safe area (A2): what is left of the map between the header + chip row and the open sheet. Both are SET AT RUNTIME on .ff-screen by App, from the real layout (the topbar's bottom edge; the sheet's height while it is open, 0 when closed) -- these are only the first-paint defaults. Every pan or zoom that targets a pin centres it between the two, and the map's pan limits run past the festival by the same amounts so any pin can get there.

rules.statement: No tap target overlaps another at any of the three zoom stops, on either map, or on paper. Circles may touch edge to edge; they may not cross. When two collide, either the lower-priority pin waits for a closer stop (from: 'detail' in pins.js) or the two are moved edge to edge.
priority: water, beverage stations, PTA, food carts
rules.reason: An overlap invites a wrong tap, and paper has no zoom to hide behind.
enforcedBy: e2e: no two touch targets overlap at the
e2e: on, no two touch targets overlap at the
e2e: print: nothing covers anything else
rules.source: CLAUDE.md › Decided — don't reopen › No element covers another

rules.statement: --tap-min (44px) is the floor for every control (chips, close, zoom buttons, the ItemPager's buttons, the handle); --pin-hit (44px) is the hit area centred on every pin. The visible glyph may be smaller than its target; the target may not.
rules.reason: 44 CSS px is 44pt on iPhone, Apple's HIG minimum; WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8 asks for 24px with a spacing exception, which the no-overlap rule satisfies for pins.
enforcedBy: e2e: zoom button is --tap-min (44px)
e2e: B2 both ItemPager buttons are --tap-min
e2e: B4 the x is right-aligned and at least --tap-min
e2e: the handle is a 44px grab area
rules.source: CLAUDE.md › Decided — don't reopen › Pins are touch targets. 44×44 CSS px is the floor.

rules.statement: A value that isn't a token becomes a token, documented in design-system.html, before it is used. Components reference only semantic and component tokens (tiers 2 and 3); a raw hex in a component is a bug.
rules.reason: The design system grows alongside the build instead of being reverse-documented afterward.
enforcedBy: ds: npm run ds -- check reports raw hex and px values that have a token, and tokens that do not exist (on a snippet; advisory)
review
rules.source: CLAUDE.md › Build with components and reference the design system on every move

rules.statement: One name per component, used the same way everywhere: in the code, the CSS (.ffc-<name>), the tests, the docs and the design-system page. The Names table in design-system.html §3 is the list; check it before adding a class or a word for something, and fix a stray old name when you see one. The component is ItemPager, never "pager", "stepper" or "booth nav".
rules.reason: A person, an agent and a grep should all find the same thing under the same word.
enforcedBy: ci: manifest is current
ds: npm run ds -- check reports a class that is not in the Names table
review
rules.source: CLAUDE.md › One name per component, used the same way everywhere

rules.statement: Close is always top-right, on the first row under the handle, in every sheet state. A top-level sheet's first row is its title line; a pushed detail's is the ‹ back row, with the booth's own title on the row below.
rules.reason: It never moves when the content does, and the thumb always knows where it is.
enforcedBy: e2e: the x is on the first row under the handle in all
e2e: the x holds one right edge in every state
e2e: a pushed booth has back at the left on the x's row
rules.source: CLAUDE.md › Close is always top-right, on the first row under the handle

rules.statement: The way you step in is the way you step out: one layer per back. A booth opened from a list pushes in from the right and ‹ back pops it to the right with the height held; the ItemPager pages sideways and never adds a step. The phone's back gesture closes the sheet first, then clears the chip, then leaves the page.
rules.reason: Every way in has exactly one way out, so no gesture skips a layer or adds one.
enforcedBy: e2e: item 4.1: back with a sheet open closes the sheet and stays on the map
e2e: item 4.1: back again clears the chip, still on the map
e2e: item 4.5: back returns to that list
rules.source: CLAUDE.md › the way you step in is the way you step out

rules.statement: A number on paper has to point at a list row. The three food carts are C1–C3 (n on the cart's pin, the one place); food-stall numbers are off the printed map.
rules.reason: A printed number with no row to look up in is noise on a one-page handout.
enforcedBy: e2e: print: every art booth square carries its number, and no stall does
